name: Jordan
summary: Muslim estates follow Sharia fixed shares, and a bequest cannot go beyond one third. Difference of religion bars inheritance (Personal Status Law 2019, art. 281/B). The sources found do not cover non-Muslim foreigners, trusts or foundations, so those answers are provisional.
reserved_share: Muslims: Sharia fixed shares under the Personal Status Law 2019; religion is a bar to inheriting (art. 281/B); bequests are capped at one third of the estate (stated by Jordan's Iftaa Department, not the statute text).
foreign_law_note: No source found on how Jordanian courts treat the estate of a non-Muslim foreigner or whether the national law applies. Christian communities have their own personal-status courts in Jordan (not sourced here).
trust_note: No trust statute and no private-foundation law were found; Islamic waqf and charities exist but were not researched. Both answers are provisional, 'no' because nothing was found.
open_questions: Jordan's conflict rule for foreigners' estates (Civil Code) not found.
Whether Jordan has any trust or private-foundation law (and the status of family waqf) not found.
One-third cap is sourced to a fatwa, not the 2019 law.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.

sources.title: Personal Status Law (2019) art. 281: difference of religion (Jordan Iftaa fatwa)
